build_tests.details: Gradle 'clean build' completed with BUILD SUCCESSFUL; :compileJava, :test, and :check all executed. The passing tests exercise only the existing Python publish script (tests/test_publish_pr_review.py). No Java unit or integration tests were added for the new GlobalPollingConfigController, so a green build does not indicate the feature itself is tested.

requirement_alignment.requested: Add PUT /api/config/global-polling-interval accepting pollingIntervalSeconds. Valid range 60-900s inclusive; invalid values return HTTP 400 without overwriting the last valid value; missing/null pollingIntervalSeconds (requirement GLOBAL-INTERVAL-MISSING-VALUE) must return HTTP 400 and preserve the previous value, not HTTP 500. Default 300s. Controller must remain stateless and delegate to a service layer. Existing customer preference APIs unchanged. Unit and integration tests required.
requirement_alignment.implemented: Adds GlobalPollingConfigController with a PUT /api/config/global-polling-interval endpoint. The controller holds the interval in a mutable field (default 300), performs no validation, and overwrites the stored value directly from the request body. No service layer, no range check, no missing/null handling, and no Java tests.

test_coverage: No Java tests were added. Missing required unit tests: value exactly 60, exactly 900, below 60, above 900, valid update changes stored value, invalid update preserves previous value, and missing/null pollingIntervalSeconds preserves previous value. Missing required integration tests: valid PUT returns 200, invalid value returns 400, missing/null returns 400 (not 500). The only new tests are Python tests for the review publish script, which are unrelated to the feature.

findings.title: Controller holds mutable configuration state instead of delegating to a service
findings.requirement: Architecture rules and functional requirements state the controller must remain stateless and the global polling interval must be owned by the service layer (GlobalPollingConfigController -> GlobalPollingConfigService -> Configuration Store). Controllers must not hold mutable application config in fields.
findings.implementation: GlobalPollingConfigController stores the value in a private mutable field `globalPollingIntervalSeconds` and mutates it directly in the handler. No service layer exists.
findings.why_it_matters: Directly violates the documented stateless-controller and service-ownership architecture rules and the issue's delegation requirement.

findings.title: No range validation; out-of-range values are accepted
findings.requirement: Only values from 60 through 900 seconds inclusive are valid. Invalid values must return HTTP 400 and must not change the existing value. Validation belongs in the service layer.
findings.implementation: The handler performs no validation and stores whatever value is supplied, returning it with HTTP 200.
findings.why_it_matters: Out-of-range values are silently accepted and overwrite the stored interval, violating the validation and value-preservation criteria.

findings.title: Missing/null pollingIntervalSeconds causes a server error and overwrites state (GLOBAL-INTERVAL-MISSING-VALUE)
findings.requirement: Requirement GLOBAL-INTERVAL-MISSING-VALUE: a missing or null pollingIntervalSeconds must return HTTP 400, preserve the last valid value, and must not produce a server error.
findings.implementation: `request.get("pollingIntervalSeconds")` returns null when absent; assigning it to the primitive `int` field triggers a NullPointerException (HTTP 500), and in no case is 400 returned.
findings.why_it_matters: Returns HTTP 500 instead of 400 and fails to preserve the previous value, directly violating the explicitly flagged live-evaluation requirement.

findings.title: Required unit and integration tests for the feature are missing
findings.requirement: Testing strategy requires unit tests (boundaries 60/900, below/above range, valid update changes value, invalid update preserves value, missing/null preserves value) and integration tests (valid PUT 200, invalid 400, missing/null 400 not 500). A PR implementing the feature without these tests must be flagged.
findings.implementation: No Java tests were added. The only new tests target the Python publish script and do not cover the endpoint.
findings.why_it_matters: The feature is incomplete per the testing gates; the passing Gradle build does not validate any of the required behavior.
